source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 3
entries.text: Ge 49:3, 4 . Reuben forfeited by his crime the rights and honors of primogeniture. His posterity never made any figure; no judge, prophet, nor ruler, sprang from this tribe.

entries.heading: Verse 5
entries.text: Ge 49:5-7 . Simeon and Levi were associate in wickedness, and the same prediction would be equally applicable to both their tribes. Levi had cities allotted to them ( Jos 21:1-45 ) in every tribe. On account of their zeal against idolatry, they were honorably "divided in Jacob"; whereas the tribe of Simeon, which was guilty of the grossest idolatry and the vices inseparable from it, were ignominiously "scattered."

entries.heading: Verse 8
entries.text: Ge 49:8-12 . Judah--A high pre-eminence is destined to this tribe ( Nu 10:14; Jud 1:2 ). Besides the honor of giving name to the Promised Land, David, and a greater than David--the Messiah--sprang from it. Chief among the tribes, "it grew up from a lion's whelp"--that is, a little power--till it became "an old lion"--that is, calm and quiet, yet still formidable.

entries.heading: 10. until Shiloh come
entries.text: 10. until Shiloh come --Shiloh--this obscure word is variously interpreted to mean "the sent" ( Joh 17:3 ), "the seed" ( Isa 11:1 ), the "peaceable or prosperous one" ( Eph 2:14 ) --that is, the Messiah ( Isa 11:10; Ro 15:12 ); and when He should come, "the tribe of Judah should no longer boast either an independent king or a judge of their own" [Calvin]. The Jews have been for eighteen centuries without a ruler and without a judge since Shiloh came, and "to Him the gathering of the people has been."

entries.heading: Verse 13
entries.text: Ge 49:13 . Zebulun was to have its lot on the seacoast, close to Zidon, and to engage, like that state, in maritime pursuits and commerce.

entries.heading: Verse 16
entries.text: Ge 49:16-18 . Dan--though the son of a secondary wife, was to be "as one of the tribes of Israel."

entries.heading: 17. Dan
entries.text: 17. Dan --"a judge." a serpent . . . an adder --A serpent, an adder, implies subtlety and stratagem; such was pre-eminently the character of Samson, the most illustrious of its judges.

entries.heading: Verse 19
entries.text: Ge 49:19 . Gad--This tribe should be often attacked and wasted by hostile powers on their borders ( Jud 10:8; Jer 49:1 ). But they were generally victorious in the close of their wars.

entries.heading: Verse 20
entries.text: Ge 49:20 . Asher--"Blessed." Its allotment was the seacoast between Tyre and Carmel, a district fertile in the production of the finest corn and oil in all Palestine.

entries.heading: Verse 21
entries.text: Ge 49:21 . Naphtali--The best rendering we know is this, "Naphtali is a deer roaming at liberty; he shooteth forth goodly branches," or majestic antlers [Taylor, Scripture Illustrations ], and the meaning of the prophecy seems to be that the tribe of Naphtali would be located in a territory so fertile and peaceable, that, feeding on the richest pasture, he would spread out, like a deer, branching antlers.

entries.heading: 28. all these are the twelve tribes of Israel
entries.text: 28. all these are the twelve tribes of Israel --or ancestors. Jacob's prophetic words obviously refer not so much to the sons as to the tribes of Israel.

entries.heading: 29. he charged them
entries.text: 29. he charged them --The charge had already been given and solemnly undertaken ( Ge 47:31 ). But in mentioning his wishes now and rehearsing all the circumstances connected with the purchase of Machpelah, he wished to declare, with his latest breath, before all his family, that he died in the same faith as Abraham.

entries.heading: 33. when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons
entries.text: 33. when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons --It is probable that he was supernaturally strengthened for this last momentous office of the patriarch, and that when the divine afflatus ceased, his exhausted powers giving way, he yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.
